correctness.rationale: An explicit integer rank labels every two-element state set bijectively from 1 to binomial(n,2). For the cyclic letter, non-head ranks fall by exactly one and layer heads wrap to larger ranks. For the other letter, precisely layer heads decrease rank by one, while all other pairs are fixed or increase. Therefore every action decreases rank by at most one and each pair has exactly one rank-decreasing action. The descending path is a unique shortest merging word, and its concatenated layer pattern proves the suffix master formula for all n>=2. The independent transition-graph reverse BFS and path-count program checked all pairs for n=2..80. Boundary n=2 and even diametrical case are proved, not extrapolated from computation.

originality.rationale: The known extremal pair distance N in an N-vertex pair graph already implies the unlabelled spectrum 1,...,N, because a shortest N-step route must traverse every pair before reaching a singleton. That spectrum is NOT claimed to be new. The candidate adds two assertions not entailed by this extremal argument: the explicit labeled formula identifying which pair realizes each rank, and uniqueness of the shortest merging word from every pair, equivalently a single explicit master-suffix chain. The inspected primary literature and indexed scientific records did not show these stronger claims. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment with a stated risk of historical equivalent presentations.

value.rationale: The Černý family is the canonical extremal synchronizing automaton, and shortest merging sequences of individual pairs form the fundamental shortest-path forest in reset algorithms. The known maximum forces the abstract 1..N spectrum and is not credited as new value. The motivated new information is the explicit rank of each labeled pair and the global rigidity: every one of their shortest merging words is unique and equal to a distinct suffix of one explicit word. This describes the exact optimal control from every pair for all n, not just a hard witness or a numerical sample.
